translations.literal: In the second month of the second year of Tiansheng under Renzong, Vice Commissioner of Honored Ceremonies and Huimin River patrol officer Tian Chengshuo submitted a proposal: rebuild the Heliu Town Great Flow Weir sluice gate at Xuzhou, newly open a flood-reduction channel for transport, saving five hundred li of detour.
translations.idiomatic: In the second month of the second year of Tiansheng, Tian Chengshuo, Vice Commissioner of Honored Ceremonies and patrol officer of the Huimin River, proposed rebuilding the Great Flow Weir sluice at Heliu Town in Xuzhou, opening a flood-reduction channel for transport that would shorten the route by five hundred li.

sentences.zh: 詔遣使按視以聞。

translations.literal: An edict ordered envoys sent to inspect and report.
translations.idiomatic: The court ordered an inspection and report.

sentences.zh: 五年八月，都大巡護惠民河王克基言：「先准宣惠民、京、索河水淺小，緣出源西京、鄭、許州界，惠民河下合橫溝、白雁溝、京、索河下合西河、湖河、雙河、欒霸河、丈八溝，各為民間裁水蒔稻灌園，宜令州縣巡察。」

translations.literal: In the eighth month of the fifth year, Chief Huimin River patrol officer Wang Keji said: "Previously approved because Huimin, Jing, and Suo river waters were shallow — originating in Xijing and Zheng and Xu prefecture boundaries — below the Huimin River the Henggou, Jianbaiyan Ditch, Jing and Suo rivers below combine Xi River, Hu River, Shuang River, Luanba River, and Zhangba Ditch; each is cut by commoners for rice planting and garden irrigation — counties and prefectures should be ordered to patrol."
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth month of the fifth year, Wang Keji, chief patrol officer of the Huimin River, reported: "Because the Huimin, Jing, and Suo rivers run low — their sources lying in Xijing and the Zheng and Xu prefectures — local farmers divert water from the Henggou, Jianbaiyan Ditch, and from the Xi, Hu, Shuang, Luanba, and Zhangba rivers below the Jing and Suo for rice and irrigation. Prefectures and counties should be ordered to patrol and enforce the regulations."

sentences.zh: 七年，王克基言：「按舊制，蔡河斗門棧板須依時啟閉，調停水勢。」

translations.literal: In the seventh year, Wang Keji said: "According to old regulations, Cai River sluice gate plank bars must be opened and closed according to season to regulate water force."
translations.idiomatic: In the seventh year Wang Keji reported: "Under longstanding regulations, the plank gates on the Cai River sluices must be opened and closed seasonally to balance the flow."

sentences.zh: 嘉祐三年正月，開京城西葛家岡新河，以有司言：「至和中，大水入京城，請自祥符縣界葛家岡開生河，直城南好草陂，北入惠民河，分注魯溝，以紓京城之患。」

translations.literal: In the first month of the third year of Jiayou, the new Gejiagang River west of the capital was opened — because officials said: "In the Zhihe era, great flood entered the capital; it was requested to open a new channel from Gejiagang at the Xiangfu County boundary, straight to Haocao Pond south of the city, north into the Huimin River, dividing into Lugou — to relieve the capital's calamity."
translations.idiomatic: In the first month of the third year of Jiayou, the new Gejiagang Canal west of the capital was opened on officials' recommendation: "During the Zhihe era, floodwaters entered the capital; they proposed opening a channel from Gejiagang on the Xiangfu County border, running straight to Haocao Pond south of the city, then north into the Huimin River and branching into the Lugou — to ease flooding in the capital."

sentences.zh: 神宗熙寧四年七月，程昉請開宋家等堤，畎水以助漕運。

translations.literal: In the seventh month of the fourth year of Xining under Shenzong, Cheng Fang requested opening the Song family and other dikes, channeling water to assist transport.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventh month of the fourth year of Xining, Cheng Fang requested opening dikes at Songjia and elsewhere to channel water and support grain transport.

sentences.zh: 八月，三班借職楊琰請增置上下壩閘，蓄水備淺涸。

translations.literal: In the eighth month, Yang Yan, provisional clerk of the Third Rank, requested adding upper and lower dam sluices to store water against shoals and drought.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth month, Yang Yan, a provisional clerk of the Third Rank, requested additional upper and lower dam sluices to store water against shallow stretches and drought.

sentences.zh: 詔琰掌其事。

translations.literal: An edict put Yan in charge of the matter.
translations.idiomatic: Yang Yan was put in charge of the project.

sentences.zh: 六年九月戊辰，將作監尚宗儒言：「議者請置蔡河木岸，計功頗大。」

translations.literal: On day wuchen in the ninth month of the sixth year, Director of Palace Construction Shang Zongru said: "Memorialists request wooden banks on the Cai River — calculated labor is quite large."
translations.idiomatic: On the wuchen day of the ninth month of the sixth year, Shang Zongru of the Directorate of Palace Construction reported: "Some have proposed timber revetments along the Cai River, but the labor required would be considerable."

sentences.zh: 詔修固土岸。

translations.literal: An edict ordered repairing solid earthen banks instead.
translations.idiomatic: The court ordered solid earthen banks built instead.

sentences.zh: 八年，詔京西運米于河北，於是侯叔獻請因丁字河故道鑿堤置閘，引汴水入于蔡，以通舟運。

translations.literal: In the eighth year, an edict ordered transporting grain from Jingxi to Hebei; thereupon Hou Shuxian requested using the old T-shaped river course to cut dikes and set sluices, drawing Bian water into the Cai for boat transport.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth year the court ordered grain transported from Jingxi to Hebei; Hou Shuxian then proposed cutting sluices along the old T-shaped channel to draw Bian water into the Cai for shipping.

sentences.zh: 河成，舟不可行，尋廢。

translations.literal: The river was completed but boats could not travel; soon it was abandoned.
translations.idiomatic: The canal was completed, but boats could not use it, and the project was soon abandoned.

sentences.zh: 十月，詔都水監展惠民河，欲便修城也。

translations.literal: In the tenth month, an edict ordered the Directorate of Waterworks to extend the Huimin River — intending to facilitate wall repair.
translations.idiomatic: In the tenth month the Directorate of Waterworks was ordered to widen the Huimin River to facilitate wall repairs.

sentences.zh: 九年七月，提轄修京城所請引霧澤陂水至咸豐門，合京、索河，由京、索簽入副堤河，下合惠民。

translations.literal: In the seventh month of the ninth year, the Capital Repair Office requested drawing Wuzepo pool water to Xianfeng Gate, joining Jing and Suo rivers, by Jing and Suo spur entering the secondary dike river, downstream joining Huimin.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventh month of the ninth year, the Capital Repair Office proposed diverting water from Wuzepo Pool to Xianfeng Gate, joining the Jing and Suo rivers and entering the secondary dike channel by a spur from the Jing and Suo, thence to the Huimin.

sentences.zh: 都水監謂：「不若於順天門外簽直河身，及於染院後簽入護龍河，至咸豐門南復入京、索河，實為長利。」

translations.literal: The Directorate of Waterworks said: "Better to spur straight from the channel outside Shuntian Gate, and behind the Dye Works spur into the Protect-the-Dragon River, south of Xianfeng Gate re-entering Jing and Suo rivers — truly a lasting benefit."
translations.idiomatic: The Directorate of Waterworks countered: "It would be better to cut a spur from the main channel outside Shuntian Gate and another behind the Dye Works into the Protect-the-Dragon River, rejoining the Jing and Suo south of Xianfeng Gate — a plan of lasting benefit."

sentences.zh: 從之。

translations.literal: This was approved.
translations.idiomatic: This proposal was approved.

sentences.zh: 廣濟河導菏水，自開封曆陳留、曹、濟、鄆，其廣五丈，歲漕上供米六十二萬石。

translations.literal: The Guangji River guides He water from Kaifeng through Chenliu, Cao, Ji, and Yun — its width five zhang; annually it transports tribute grain of six hundred and twenty thousand shi.
translations.idiomatic: The Guangji River draws He River water from Kaifeng through Chenliu, Cao, Ji, and Yun; five zhang wide, it transported six hundred and twenty thousand shi of tribute grain each year.

sentences.zh: 太祖建隆二年正月，遣使往定陶規度，發曹、單丁夫數萬浚之。

translations.literal: In the first month of the second year of Jianlong under Taizu, envoys were sent to Dingtao to survey; tens of thousands of laborers from Cao and Shan were mobilized to dredge it.
translations.idiomatic: In the first month of the second year of Jianlong, envoys were sent to Dingtao to survey the route, and tens of thousands of laborers from Cao and Shan were mobilized to dredge the canal.

sentences.zh: 三月，幸新水門觀放水入河。

translations.literal: In the third month, the emperor visited the New Water Gate to observe water released into the river.
translations.idiomatic: In the third month the emperor visited the New Water Gate to watch water released into the canal.

sentences.zh: 先是，五丈河泥淤，不利行舟。

translations.literal: Earlier, the Wuzhang River was muddy and silted, unfavorable for boats.
translations.idiomatic: Previously the Wuzhang River had silted up with mud, impeding navigation.

sentences.zh: 遂詔左監門衛將軍陳承昭於京城之西，夾汴水造斗門，引京、索、蔡河水通城濠入斗門，俾架流汴水之上，東進於五丈河，以便東北漕運。

translations.literal: Thereupon an edict ordered Left Gate Guard General Chen Chengzhao at the west of the capital to build sluice gates flanking the Bian, drawing Jing, Suo, and Cai river water through the moat into the sluice gates, raising flow above the Bian water, advancing east into the Wuzhang River — to facilitate northeast transport.
translations.idiomatic: The court ordered Chen Chengzhao, general of the Left Gate Guard, to build sluice gates west of the capital flanking the Bian, drawing water from the Jing, Suo, and Cai rivers through the moat into the gates and lifting it above the Bian to flow east into the Wuzhang River, easing northeast grain transport.

sentences.zh: 公私鹹利。

translations.literal: Public and private all benefited.
translations.idiomatic: Both the government and private parties profited.

sentences.zh: 三年正月，遣右龍武統軍陳承昭護修五丈河役，車駕臨視，賜承昭錢二十萬。

translations.literal: In the first month of the third year, Right Dragon Martial Commanding General Chen Chengzhao was sent to oversee Wuzhang River labor; the imperial carriage visited to inspect; Chen Chengzhao was granted two hundred thousand in cash.
translations.idiomatic: In the first month of the third year, Chen Chengzhao, commanding general of the Right Dragon Martial Guard, was sent to supervise repairs on the Wuzhang River; the emperor visited in person and granted him two hundred thousand cash.

sentences.zh: 乾德三年，京師引五丈河造西水磑。

translations.literal: In the third year of Qiande, the capital drew the Wuzhang River to build the Xishui mill.
translations.idiomatic: In the third year of Qiande, the capital tapped the Wuzhang River to power the Xishui mill.

sentences.zh: 太宗太平興國三年正月，命發近縣丁夫浚廣濟河。

translations.literal: In the first month of the third year of Taiping Xingguo under Taizong, nearby county laborers were ordered mobilized to dredge the Guangji River.
translations.idiomatic: In the first month of the third year of Taiping Xingguo, laborers from nearby counties were mobilized to dredge the Guangji River.

sentences.zh: 真宗景德二年六月，開封府言：「京西沿汴萬勝鎮，先置斗門，以減河水，今汴河分注濁水入廣濟河，堙塞不利。」

translations.literal: In the sixth month of the second year of Jingde under Zhenzong, Kaifeng Prefecture said: "At Wansheng Town along the Bian in western Jing, sluice gates were previously placed to reduce river water; now the Bian divides and pours muddy water into the Guangji River — blocking is unfavorable."
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth month of the second year of Jingde, Kaifeng Prefecture reported: "At Wansheng Town on the Bian in western Jing, sluice gates were installed to reduce the river flow; now the Bian pours muddy water into the Guangji River, and blocking the gates would impede drainage."

sentences.zh: 帝曰：「此斗門本李繼源所造，屢詢利害，以為始因京、索河遇雨即泛流入汴，遂置斗門，以便通泄。

translations.literal: The emperor said: "These sluice gates were originally made by Li Jiyuan; the pros and cons were repeatedly inquired — it was thought that initially because Jing and Suo rivers when encountering rain immediately overflowed into the Bian, therefore sluice gates were placed for convenient discharge.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor replied: "These sluice gates were built by Li Jiyuan. I have repeatedly asked about their merits and drawbacks. They were originally installed because rain on the Jing and Suo rivers caused floodwater to pour into the Bian; the gates were meant to ease that discharge.

sentences.zh: 若遽壅塞，復慮決溢。」

translations.literal: If hurriedly blocked, again fear breach and overflow."
translations.idiomatic: To block them abruptly would risk fresh breaches and overflows."

sentences.zh: 因令多用巨石，高置斗門，水雖甚大，而餘波亦可減去。

translations.literal: He therefore ordered many large stones used, sluice gates set high — though water was very great, the remaining waves could also be reduced.
translations.idiomatic: He therefore ordered larger stones used and the sluice gates set higher, so that even in heavy flood the surplus water could still be drawn off.

sentences.zh: 三年，內侍趙守倫建議：自京東分廣濟河由定陶至徐州入清河，以達江、湖漕路。

translations.literal: In the third year, Palace Attendant Zhao Shoulun proposed: branching the Guangji River from Jingdong through Dingtao to Xuzhou and entering the Qing River, to reach the Jiang and Hu lake transport routes.
translations.idiomatic: In the third year, Palace Attendant Zhao Shoulun proposed branching the Guangji River from Jingdong through Dingtao to Xuzhou and into the Qing River, thereby reaching the grain routes of the Yangzi region and the lakes.

sentences.zh: 役既成，遣使覆視，繪圖來上。

translations.literal: When the labor was completed, envoys were sent to reinspect, and maps were submitted.
translations.idiomatic: When the work was finished, the court sent envoys to reinspect the project and submit maps.

sentences.zh: 帝以地有隆阜，而水勢極淺，雖置堰埭，又曆呂梁灘磧之險，非可漕運，罷之。

translations.literal: The emperor held that the terrain had elevated mounds and the water was extremely shallow; even with weirs and dams placed, it would also pass the dangerous shoals of Lüliang — not feasible for transport — and cancelled it.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor judged that the ground rose in mounds and the water was far too shallow; even with weirs and dams, the route would still have to pass the treacherous shoals at Lüliang and could not serve grain transport, so the project was abandoned.

sentences.zh: 仁宗天聖六年七月，尚書駕部員外郎閻貽慶言：「五丈河下接濟州之合蔡鎮，通利梁山濼。

translations.literal: In the seventh month of the sixth year of Tiansheng under Renzong, Assistant Director in the Ministry of Imperial Chariots Yan Yiqing said: "The Wuzhang River below connects to Hechai Town in Jizhou, benefiting passage to Liangshan Marsh.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventh month of the sixth year of Tiansheng, Yan Yiqing, assistant director in the Ministry of Imperial Chariots, reported: "The Wuzhang River below joins Hechai Town in Jizhou and eases access to Liangshan Marsh.

sentences.zh: 近者天河決蕩，溺民田，壞道路，合蔡而下，漫散不通舟，請治五丈河入夾黃河。」

translations.literal: Recently the Tian River burst and flooded, drowning civilian fields and ruining roads; below Hechai it spread diffusely and boats could not pass — request dredging the Wuzhang River to enter the flanking Yellow River."
translations.idiomatic: Recently the Tian River broke its banks, flooded farmland, and destroyed roads; below Hechai the waters spread so widely that boats could no longer pass. I ask that the Wuzhang River be dredged to join the Yellow River channel."

sentences.zh: 因詔貽慶與水官李守忠規度，計功料以聞。

translations.literal: Thereupon Yan Yiqing and the water official Li Shouzhong were ordered to survey and calculate labor and materials for report.
translations.idiomatic: The court then ordered Yan Yiqing and the waterworks official Li Shouzhong to survey the site, estimate labor and materials, and report back.

sentences.zh: 神宗熙寧七年，趙濟言：「河淺廢運，自此物賤傷農，宜議興復，以便公私。」

translations.literal: In the seventh year of Xining under Shenzong, Zhao Ji said: "The river is shallow and transport abandoned; from this goods are cheap and farmers harmed — restoration should be discussed for public and private convenience."
translations.idiomatic: In the seventh year of Xining, Zhao Ji argued: "The river has grown too shallow for transport to continue; goods are cheap and farmers suffer as a result. We should discuss restoring the route for the benefit of both the state and private trade."

sentences.zh: 詔張士澄、楊琰修治。

translations.literal: An edict ordered Zhang Shicheng and Yang Yan to repair it.
translations.idiomatic: The court ordered Zhang Shicheng and Yang Yan to carry out repairs.

sentences.zh: 八月，都提舉汴河堤岸司言：「欲於通津門汴河岸東城裏三十步內開河，下通廣濟，以便行運。」

translations.literal: In the eighth month, the Directorate General for Bian River Embankments said: "We wish to open a canal within thirty paces inside the city wall east of the Bian at Tongjin Gate, leading down to connect with the Guangji, to facilitate transport."
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth month, the directorate general for Bian River embankments proposed: "We wish to cut a canal within thirty paces inside the eastern city wall at Tongjin Gate on the Bian, linking it down to the Guangji to ease transport."

sentences.zh: 從之。

translations.literal: It was approved.
translations.idiomatic: The proposal was approved.

sentences.zh: 八年，又遣琰同陳祐甫因汴河置滲水塘，又自孫賈斗門置虛堤八，滲水入西賈陂，由減水河注霧澤陂，皆為河之上源。

translations.literal: In the eighth year, Yang Yan was again sent with Chen Youfu to install seepage ponds along the Bian; also from Sunjia sluice gate eight hollow dikes were placed, seepage entering Xijia Reservoir, by the flood-reduction river pouring into Wuzhe Reservoir — all as upper sources for the river.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth year, Yang Yan was again sent with Chen Youfu to build seepage ponds along the Bian. Eight hollow dikes were also placed at the Sunjia sluice gate so that seepage would enter Xijia Reservoir and, through the flood-reduction canal, feed Wuzhe Reservoir — all serving as upper sources for the canal.

sentences.zh: 九年，詔依元額漕粟京東，仍修壩閘，為啟閉之節。

translations.literal: In the ninth year, an edict ordered grain transport from Jingdong according to the original quota, still repairing dams and gates for opening and closing regulation.
translations.idiomatic: In the ninth year, an edict ordered grain shipments from Jingdong to resume at the original quota and directed that dams and sluice gates be repaired to regulate opening and closing.

sentences.zh: 九年三月，詔遣官修廣濟河壩閘。

translations.literal: In the third month of the ninth year, officials were ordered dispatched to repair Guangji River dams and gates.
translations.idiomatic: In the third month of the ninth year, the court dispatched officials to repair the dams and sluice gates on the Guangji River.

sentences.zh: 元豐五年三月癸亥，罷廣濟輦運司，移上供物自淮陽軍界入汴，以清河輦運司為名，命張士澄都大提舉。

translations.literal: On the guihai day of the third month of the fifth year of Yuanfeng, the Guangji Transport Directorate was abolished; tribute goods were shifted to enter the Bian from the Huaiyang Army boundary, named the Qinghe Transport Directorate, with Zhang Shicheng appointed as director general.
translations.idiomatic: On the guihai day of the third month in the fifth year of Yuanfeng, the Guangji Transport Directorate was abolished. Tribute goods were rerouted from the Huaiyang Army boundary into the Bian, and the office was renamed the Qinghe Transport Directorate, with Zhang Shicheng appointed as its director general.

sentences.zh: 七月，御史王植言：「廣濟安流而上，與清河溯流入汴，遠近險易較然，廢之非是。」

translations.literal: In the seventh month, Censor Wang Zhi said: "The Guangji flows smoothly upstream while the Qing requires upstream entry into the Bian — distance and difficulty clearly compared — abolishing it is wrong."
translations.idiomatic: In the seventh month, Censor Wang Zhi argued: "The Guangji carries boats smoothly upstream, whereas the Qing route requires laborious upstream entry into the Bian. The difference in distance and difficulty is obvious, and abolishing the Guangji was a mistake."

sentences.zh: 詔監司詳議。

translations.literal: Supervisory officials were ordered to deliberate in detail.
translations.idiomatic: The court ordered supervisory officials to examine the matter in detail.

sentences.zh: 七年八月，都大提舉汴河堤岸司言：「京東地富，穀粟可漕，獨患河澀。

translations.literal: In the eighth month of the seventh year, the Bian River Embankments Directorate General said: "Jingdong land is rich and grain can be transported — the sole problem is sluggish river flow.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth month of the seventh year, the directorate general for Bian River embankments reported: "Jingdong is fertile and its grain can be shipped by water; the only problem is that the river runs sluggishly.

sentences.zh: 若因修京城，令役兵近汴穴土，使之成渠，就引河水注之廣濟，則漕舟可通，是一舉而兩利也。」

translations.literal: If, by reason of capital repairs, corvée soldiers near the Bian dig earth forming a channel and lead river water into the Guangji, transport boats can pass — one measure, twofold benefit."
translations.idiomatic: If, while the capital is being repaired, corvée troops near the Bian were made to dig out earth and form a channel, and Bian water were then led into the Guangji, transport boats could pass — a single project with a double benefit."

sentences.zh: 從之。

translations.literal: It was approved.
translations.idiomatic: The proposal was approved.

sentences.zh: 哲宗元祐元年，詔斥祥符霧澤陂募民承佃，增置水匱。

translations.literal: In the first year of Yuanyou under Zhezong, an edict ordered clearing Xiangfu Wuzhe Reservoir, recruiting civilians to lease cultivation, and adding water storage.
translations.idiomatic: In the first year of Yuanyou, an edict ordered the Xiangfu Wuzhe Reservoir drained, leased out to civilians for cultivation, and supplemented with additional water storage.

sentences.zh: 又即宣澤門外仍舊引京、索源河，置槽架水，流入咸豐門。

translations.literal: Also at Xuanye Gate outside, still drawing the Jing and Suo source rivers, placing trough frames for water, flowing into Xianfeng Gate.
translations.idiomatic: Outside Xuanye Gate, the Jing and Suo source rivers were again tapped as before, water was raised by trough frames, and the flow was directed into Xianfeng Gate.

sentences.zh: 皆以為廣濟淺澀之備。

translations.literal: All were as preparation for the Guangji's shallow sluggishness.
translations.idiomatic: All of this was intended as a reserve against the Guangji's shallowness and sluggish flow.

sentences.zh: 三月，三省言：「廣濟河輦運，近因言者廢罷，改置清河輦運，迂遠不便。」

translations.literal: In the third month, the Three Departments said: "Guangji River transport — recently abolished upon remonstrators' advice, replaced with Qinghe transport — circuitous and inconvenient."
translations.idiomatic: In the third month, the Three Departments reported: "Guangji River transport was recently abolished after critics spoke out and was replaced by Qinghe transport, which is roundabout and inconvenient."

sentences.zh: 詔知棣州王諤措置興復。

translations.literal: Prefect of Dizhou Wang E was ordered to arrange restoration.
translations.idiomatic: The court ordered Wang E, prefect of Dizhou, to arrange its restoration.

sentences.zh: 都水監亦言：「廣濟河以京、索河為源，轉漕京東歲計。

translations.literal: The Directorate of Waterworks also said: "The Guangji River takes the Jing and Suo rivers as source, transferring Jingdong annual grain quota.
translations.idiomatic: The Directorate of Waterworks also reported: "The Guangji River draws its water from the Jing and Suo rivers and carries Jingdong's annual grain quota.

sentences.zh: 今欲依舊，即令于宣澤門外置槽架水，流入咸豐門裏，由舊河道復廣濟河源，以通漕運。」

translations.literal: Now wishing to follow old practice, immediately order trough frames for water placed outside Xuanye Gate, flowing inside Xianfeng Gate, restoring Guangji source by the old channel, to open transport."
translations.idiomatic: To restore the old arrangement, trough frames should again be placed outside Xuanye Gate to raise water and send it inside Xianfeng Gate, and the Guangji's headwaters should be reopened along the former channel so that transport can resume."

sentences.zh: 從之。

translations.literal: It was approved.
translations.idiomatic: The proposal was approved.

sentences.zh: 金水河一名天源，本京水，導自滎陽黃堆山，其源曰祝龍泉。

translations.literal: The Jinshui River, also called Tianyuan, was originally the Jing River, led from Huangdui Mountain in Xingyang; its source is called Zhulong Spring.
translations.idiomatic: The Jinshui River, also known as Tianyuan, was originally the Jing River. It was diverted from Huangdui Mountain in Xingyang, and its source is called Zhulong Spring.

sentences.zh: 太祖建隆二年春，命左領軍衛上將軍陳承昭率水工鑿渠，引水過中牟，名曰金水河，凡百餘里，抵都城西，架其水橫絕於汴，設斗門，入浚溝，通城濠，東匯於五丈河。

translations.literal: In spring of the second year of Jianlong under Taizu, Left Army Guard Senior General Chen Chengzhao was ordered to lead waterworkers to cut a canal, leading water past Zhongmou, named Jinshui River, over a hundred li, reaching west of the capital, raising its water across the Bian, setting sluice gates, entering the Jun ditch, connecting the moat, east joining the Wuzhang River.
translations.idiomatic: In the spring of the second year of Jianlong, Taizu ordered Chen Chengzhao, senior general of the Left Army Guard, to lead waterworkers in cutting a canal. Water was brought past Zhongmou in a channel more than a hundred li long called the Jinshui River. Reaching the west of the capital, the flow was raised across the Bian by sluice gates, sent into the Jun ditch and the city moat, and finally joined the Wuzhang River to the east.

sentences.zh: 公私利焉。

translations.literal: Public and private benefited thereby.
translations.idiomatic: Both the government and private parties benefited from it.

sentences.zh: 乾德三年，又引貫皇城，曆後苑，內庭池沼，水皆至焉。

translations.literal: In the third year of Qiande, it was also led through the Imperial City, passing the rear garden and inner-court ponds — water reached them all.
translations.idiomatic: In the third year of Qiande, the canal was extended through the Imperial City, passing the rear gardens and the ponds of the inner court until water reached them all.

sentences.zh: 開寶九年，帝步自左掖，按地勢，命水工引金水由承天門鑿渠，為大輪激之，南注晉王第。

translations.literal: In the ninth year of Kaibao, the emperor walked from the Left Flank Gate, surveyed terrain, ordered waterworkers to lead Jinshui through Chengtian Gate cutting a canal, using a great wheel to drive it, south pouring into the Prince of Jin's mansion.
translations.idiomatic: In the ninth year of Kaibao, the emperor walked out from the Left Flank Gate, surveyed the terrain, and ordered waterworkers to cut a canal from Chengtian Gate and lead the Jinshui through it. A great wheel was used to lift the water and send it south into the mansion of the Prince of Jin.

sentences.zh: 真宗大中祥符二年九月，詔供備庫使謝德權決金水，自天波門並皇城至乾元門，曆天街東轉，繚太廟入後廟，皆甃以礲甓，植以芳木，車馬所經，又累石為間梁。

translations.literal: In the ninth month of the second year of Dazhong Xiangfu under Zhenzong, an edict ordered Provision Treasury Commissioner Xie Dequan to cut open the Jinshui, from Tianbo Gate along the Imperial City to Qianyuan Gate, passing east along Heavenly Street, circling the Grand Ancestral Temple into the Rear Temple — all paved with dressed brick, planted with fragrant trees; where carts and horses passed, stone was piled for span bridges.
translations.idiomatic: In the ninth month of the second year of Dazhong Xiangfu, an edict ordered Xie Dequan, commissioner of the Provision Treasury, to open the Jinshui. From Tianbo Gate it ran along the Imperial City to Qianyuan Gate, turned east along Heavenly Street, and circled the Grand Ancestral Temple into the Rear Temple. The channel was paved with dressed brick and lined with fragrant trees, and where carts and horses crossed, stone piers were built to carry span bridges.

sentences.zh: 作方井，官寺、民舍皆得汲用。

translations.literal: Square wells were made; government temples and civilian dwellings all could draw water.
translations.idiomatic: Square wells were built so that government offices, temples, and private houses alike could draw water.

sentences.zh: 復引東，由城下水竇入於濠。

translations.literal: It was again led east, through water passages under the city wall into the moat.
translations.idiomatic: The canal was then carried east again and, through culverts beneath the city wall, discharged into the moat.

sentences.zh: 京師便之。

translations.literal: The capital found it convenient.
translations.idiomatic: The capital greatly benefited from the arrangement.

sentences.zh: 神宗，金水河透水槽阻礙上下汴舟，遣宋用臣按視。

translations.literal: Under Shenzong, the Jinshui River overflow trough obstructed Bian boats going up and down; Song Yongchen was sent to inspect.
translations.idiomatic: Under Shenzong, the overflow trough on the Jinshui River obstructed vessels traveling up and down the Bian, and Song Yongchen was sent to inspect the problem.

sentences.zh: 請自板橋別為一河，引水北入於汴，後卒不行，乃由副堤河入于蔡。

translations.literal: He proposed opening a separate channel from Banqiao to draw water north into the Bian; this was ultimately not carried out, and water instead entered the Cai through the secondary dike channel.
translations.idiomatic: He proposed opening a separate channel from Banqiao to draw water north into the Bian, but the plan was never carried out; water instead entered the Cai through the secondary dike channel.

sentences.zh: 以源流深遠，與永安青龍河相合，故賜名曰天源。

translations.literal: Because its source stream was deep and far-reaching and it joined the Yongan Qinglong River, it was granted the name Tianyuan.
translations.idiomatic: Because its headwaters ran deep and far and it joined the Yongan Qinglong River, it was granted the name Tianyuan.

sentences.zh: 先是，舟至啟槽，頗滯舟行。

translations.literal: Earlier, when boats reached the Qicao sluice, passage was often delayed.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier, when boats reached the Qicao sluice, passage was often delayed.

sentences.zh: 既導洛通汴，遂自城西超字坊引洛水，由咸豐門立堤，凡三千三十步，水遂入禁中，而槽廢。

translations.literal: Once the Luo was guided to connect with the Bian, Luo water was drawn from Chaozifang west of the city, dikes were built at Xianfeng Gate for three thousand thirty bu, water then entered the palace precinct, and the sluice was abandoned.
translations.idiomatic: Once the Luo was guided into the Bian, Luo water was drawn from Chaozifang west of the city, dikes were built at Xianfeng Gate for three thousand thirty paces, water then entered the palace precinct, and the sluice was abandoned.

sentences.zh: 然舊惟供灑掃，至徽宗政和間，容佐請於七里河開月河一道，分減此水，灌溉內中花竹。

translations.literal: Yet formerly it served only sprinkling and sweeping; in the Zhenghe era under Huizong, Rong Zuo requested opening a crescent channel on the Qili River to divide and reduce this water and irrigate flowers and bamboo within the inner palace.
translations.idiomatic: Yet formerly it served only sprinkling and sweeping; in the Zhenghe era under Huizong, Rong Zuo requested opening a crescent channel on the Qili River to divert part of this water and irrigate flowers and bamboo within the inner palace.

sentences.zh: 命宋升措置導引，四年十一月，畢工。

translations.literal: Song Sheng was ordered to arrange the diversion; in the eleventh month of the fourth year the work was completed.
translations.idiomatic: Song Sheng was ordered to arrange the diversion, and in the eleventh month of the fourth year the work was completed.

sentences.zh: 重和元年六月，復命藍從熙、孟揆等增堤岸，置橋、槽、壩、閘，浚澄水，道水入內。

translations.literal: In the sixth month of the first year of Chonghe, Lan Congxi, Meng Kui, and others were again ordered to raise dikes and banks, set up bridges, sluices, weirs, and gates, dredge the clear water, and channel it into the inner precinct.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth month of the first year of Chonghe, Lan Congxi, Meng Kui, and others were again ordered to raise dikes and banks, set up bridges, sluices, weirs, and gates, dredge the clear water, and channel it into the inner precinct.

sentences.zh: 內庭池籞既多，患水不給，又於西南水磨引索河一派，架以石渠絕汴，南北築堤，導入天源河以助之。

translations.literal: Because the inner court had many ponds and parks and feared insufficient water supply, another branch of the Suo River was drawn from the southwestern water mill, carried across the Bian on a stone aqueduct, with dikes built north and south, and guided into the Tianyuan River to supplement it.
translations.idiomatic: Because the inner court had many ponds and parks and feared insufficient water, another branch of the Suo River was drawn from the southwestern water mill, carried across the Bian on a stone aqueduct with dikes built north and south, and guided into the Tianyuan River to supplement it.

sentences.zh: 白溝無山源，每歲水潦甚則通流，才勝百斛船，逾月不雨即竭。

translations.literal: Baigou had no mountain source; each year when floods were severe it could flow, barely supporting hundred-hu boats; more than a month without rain and it dried up.
translations.idiomatic: Baigou had no mountain headwater. In years of heavy flood it could flow, but only enough to carry boats of a hundred hu; if more than a month passed without rain, it dried up.

sentences.zh: 至道二年三月，內殿崇班閻光澤、國子博士邢用之上言：「請開白溝，自京師抵彭城呂梁口，凡六百里，以通長淮之漕。」

translations.literal: In the third month of the second year of Zhidao, Inner Hall Honored Companion Yan Guangze and National University Doctor Xing Yong submitted: "Request opening Baigou, from the capital to Lüliang mouth at Pengcheng, six hundred li total, to connect Changhuai transport."
translations.idiomatic: In the third month of the second year of Zhidao, Yan Guangze, honored companion of the Inner Hall, and Xing Yong, doctor of the National University, submitted a memorial: "We ask that Baigou be opened from the capital to Lüliang mouth at Pengcheng, six hundred li in all, to connect transport to the lower Huai."

sentences.zh: 詔發諸州丁夫數萬治之，以光澤護其役。

translations.literal: An edict mobilized tens of thousands of corvée laborers from various prefectures; Yan Guangze oversaw the labor.
translations.idiomatic: The court mobilized tens of thousands of corvée laborers from the prefectures to carry out the work and put Yan Guangze in charge of the project.

sentences.zh: 議者非之。

translations.literal: Remonstrators opposed it.
translations.idiomatic: Critics at court opposed the plan.

sentences.zh: 會宋州通判王矩上表，極陳其不可，且言：「用之田園在襄邑，歲苦水潦，私幸渠成。」

translations.literal: When Song Prefecture vice-prefect Wang Ju submitted a memorial vehemently stating its impossibility, also saying: "Yong's fields and gardens are in Xiangyi; each year he suffers floods — he privately hopes the canal succeeds."
translations.idiomatic: Then Wang Ju, vice-prefect of Song Prefecture, submitted a memorial strongly arguing that the project was impossible and adding: "Yong's fields and gardens lie in Xiangyi, where he suffers flooding every year; he privately hopes the canal will be completed for his own benefit."

sentences.zh: 遂罷其役。

translations.literal: The labor was thereupon cancelled.
translations.idiomatic: The project was thereupon abandoned.

sentences.zh: 咸平六年，用之為度支員外郎，又令自襄邑下流治白溝河，導京師積水，而民田無害。

translations.literal: In the sixth year of Xianping, Yong became Assistant Director of Revenue; again ordered from lower Xiangyi to dredge Baigou River, diverting capital accumulated water, without harming civilian fields.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth year of Xianping, after Yong became assistant director of revenue, he was again ordered to dredge the Baigou River below Xiangyi to drain accumulated water from the capital without damaging farmland.

sentences.zh: 神宗熙寧六年，都水監丞侯叔獻請儲三十六陂及京、索二水為源，仿真、楚州開平河置閘，則四時可行舟，因廢汴渠。

translations.literal: In the sixth year of Xining under Shenzong, Directorate of Waterworks Vice-Director Hou Shuxian requested storing thirty-six reservoirs and the Jing and Suo two rivers as source, modeling sluice gates on Kaiping River of Zhen and Chuzhou — then boats could travel four seasons, thereby abolishing the Bian canal.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth year of Xining, Hou Shuxian, vice-director of the Directorate of Waterworks, proposed storing water in thirty-six reservoirs and using the Jing and Suo rivers as sources. If sluice gates were built after the model of the Kaiping River in Zhen and Chuzhou, boats could travel year-round and the Bian canal could be abandoned.

sentences.zh: 帝曰：「白溝功料易耳，第汴渠歲運甚廣，河北、陝西資焉。

translations.literal: The emperor said: "Baigou labor and materials are easy — but the Bian canal's annual transport is very great; Hebei and Shaanxi depend on it.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor said: "The labor and materials for Baigou are easy enough, but the Bian canal moves a vast annual transport on which Hebei and Shaanxi depend.

sentences.zh: 又京畿公私所用良材，皆自汴口而至，何可遽廢？」

translations.literal: Also fine timber used by public and private in the capital region all arrives from the Bian mouth — how can it be abruptly abolished?"
translations.idiomatic: Moreover, the fine timber used by both public offices and private households in the capital region all comes through the Bian mouth. How can we abandon it so hastily?"

sentences.zh: 王安石曰：「此役苟成，亦無窮之利也。

translations.literal: Wang Anshi said: "If this labor succeeds, there is also boundless benefit.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Anshi replied: "If this project succeeds, the benefit will be limitless.

sentences.zh: 當別為漕河，引黃河一支，乃為經久。」

translations.literal: One should separately make a transport canal, drawing one branch of the Yellow River — that would be lasting."
translations.idiomatic: We should build a separate transport canal and draw off one branch of the Yellow River; only then will the arrangement be durable."

sentences.zh: 馮京曰：「若白溝成，與汴、蔡皆通漕，為利誠大，恐汴終不可廢。」

translations.literal: Feng Jing said: "If Baigou succeeds, with Bian and Cai all connected for transport — benefit is truly great — yet I fear the Bian can never be abolished."
translations.idiomatic: Feng Jing said: "If Baigou is completed and transport is opened on the Bian and Cai as well, the gain would indeed be great, but I fear the Bian can never truly be abandoned."

sentences.zh: 帝然之，詔劉璯同叔獻覆視。

translations.literal: The emperor agreed, ordering Liu Yan with Shuxian to reinspect.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor agreed and ordered Liu Yan to reinspect the project together with Hou Shuxian.

sentences.zh: 八月，都水監言：「白溝自濉河至於淮八百里，乞分三年興修。

translations.literal: In the eighth month, the Directorate of Waterworks said: "Baigou from the Sui River to the Huai is eight hundred li — request dividing repair over three years.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth month, the Directorate of Waterworks reported: "Baigou runs eight hundred li from the Sui River to the Huai. We ask that the work be divided over three years.

sentences.zh: 其廢汴河，俟白溝畢功，別相視。

translations.literal: Abolishing the Bian canal — wait until Baigou is completed, then separately survey.
translations.idiomatic: As for abandoning the Bian canal, that should wait until Baigou is finished and be reconsidered separately.

sentences.zh: 仍請發谷熟淤田司並京東汴河所隸河清兵赴役。」

translations.literal: Still request mobilizing Gushu Silt-Farmland Office and Hedging troops under Jingdong Bian River office for labor."
translations.idiomatic: They also asked that labor be supplied from the Gushu Silt-Farmland Office and from the river-clearing troops attached to the Jingdong Bian River office."

sentences.zh: 從之。

translations.literal: It was approved.
translations.idiomatic: The request was approved.

sentences.zh: 七年正月，都水監言：「自盟河畎導汴南諸水，近者失於疏浚，為害甚大。」

translations.literal: In the first month of the seventh year, the Directorate said: "From the Meng River channel guiding Bian-south waters — recently dredging was neglected, harm is very great."
translations.idiomatic: In the first month of the seventh year, the Directorate of Waterworks reported: "The channels that guide the waters south of the Bian from the Meng River have recently gone without dredging, causing great damage."

sentences.zh: 於是輟夫修治，而白溝之役廢。

translations.literal: Corvée labor was then halted, and the Baigou River project was abandoned.
translations.idiomatic: Labor was then halted, and the Baigou River project was abandoned.

sentences.zh: 初，王安石欲罷白溝、修汴南水利，帝曰：「人多以白溝不可為，而卿獨見可為？」

translations.literal: Initially, Wang Anshi wished to abandon Baigou and repair Bian-south waterworks; the emperor said: "Many say Baigou cannot be done — yet you alone see it can be done?"
translations.idiomatic: Earlier, when Wang Anshi wanted to abandon Baigou and repair the waterworks south of the Bian, the emperor asked: "Most people say Baigou cannot be built, yet you alone think it can?"

sentences.zh: 安石曰：「果不可為，罷之誠宜；

translations.literal: Anshi said: "If it truly cannot be done, abandoning it is indeed right;
translations.idiomatic: Anshi replied: "If it truly cannot be done, abandoning it would indeed be right;

sentences.zh: 若可為，即俟時為之，何必計校人言也。」

translations.literal: if it can be done, then wait for the time to do it — why must one calculate against people's words?"
translations.idiomatic: but if it can be done, we need only wait for the right moment to act. Why weigh every word of public opinion?"

sentences.zh: 徽宗政和二年十月，都水監丞孟昌齡言開浚含暉門外白溝河，開堰放水，仍舊通流。

translations.literal: In the tenth month of the second year of Zhenghe under Huizong, Waterworks Vice-Director Meng Changling reported opening and dredging Baigou River outside Hanhui Gate, opening weirs to release water, restoring flow as before.
translations.idiomatic: In the tenth month of the second year of Zhenghe, Meng Changling, vice-director of the Directorate of Waterworks, reported that the Baigou River outside Hanhui Gate had been opened and dredged, its weirs opened to release water, and its former flow restored.

sentences.zh: 京畿溝洫：汴都地廣平，賴溝渠以行水潦。

translations.literal: Capital-region canals and ditches: The Bian capital's land is broad and flat — it relies on canals and ditches to drain floodwater.
translations.idiomatic: Canals and ditches of the capital region: The land around the Bian capital is broad and flat, and depends on canals and ditches to carry off floodwater.

sentences.zh: 真宗景德二年五月，詔開京城濠以通舟楫，毀官水磑三所。

translations.literal: In the fifth month of the second year of Jingde under Zhenzong, an edict ordered opening the capital moat for boats, destroying three official water mills.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth month of the second year of Jingde, an edict ordered the capital moat opened for navigation and three official water mills demolished.

sentences.zh: 三年，分遣入內內侍八人，督京城內外坊裏開浚溝渠。

translations.literal: In the third year, eight Inner Palace Attendants were separately dispatched to supervise dredging canals inside and outside the capital wards.
translations.idiomatic: In the third year, eight Inner Palace attendants were dispatched separately to supervise the dredging of canals inside and outside the capital's wards.

sentences.zh: 先是，京都每歲春浚溝讀，而勢家豪族，有不即施工者。

translations.literal: Previously, the capital each spring dredged canals, but powerful families and great clans sometimes did not promptly undertake work.
translations.idiomatic: Previously the capital dredged its canals every spring, but powerful families and great clans sometimes failed to carry out the work promptly.

sentences.zh: 帝聞之，遣使分視，自是不復有稽遲者，以至雨潦暴集，無所雍遏，都人賴之。

translations.literal: The emperor heard of it, sent envoys to inspect separately — from then no more delays, so that when rain floods suddenly gathered there was no obstruction, and capital residents relied on it.
translations.idiomatic: When the emperor learned of this, he sent envoys to inspect the work in separate districts. After that there were no further delays, and when sudden rains flooded the city the waters were no longer blocked; the people of the capital benefited greatly.

sentences.zh: 大中祥符三年，遣供備庫使謝德權治溝洫，導太一宮積水抵陳留界，入亳州渦河。

translations.literal: In the third year of Dazhong Xiangfu, Provision Treasury Commissioner Xie Dequan was sent to manage canals, diverting Taiyi Palace accumulated water to Chenliu boundary, entering Bozhou Guo River.
translations.idiomatic: In the third year of Dazhong Xiangfu, Xie Dequan, commissioner of the Provision Treasury, was sent to manage the canals, diverting accumulated water from Taiyi Palace to the border of Chenliu and into the Guo River in Bozhou.

sentences.zh: 五年三月，帝宣示宰臣曰：「京師所開溝渠，雖屢鈐轄，仍令內侍分察吏擾。」

translations.literal: In the third month of the fifth year, the emperor showed and told chief ministers: "Canals opened in the capital — though repeatedly supervised — still order Inner Attendants to inspect separately against official harassment."
translations.idiomatic: In the third month of the fifth year, the emperor told his chief ministers: "Although the canals opened in the capital have been repeatedly supervised, Inner Attendants should still be sent separately to watch for official harassment."

sentences.zh: 仁宗天聖元年八月，東西八作司與內殿承制、閣門祗候劉永崇等言：「內外八廂創置八字水口，通流兩水入渠甚利，慮所置處豪富及勢要阻抑，乞下令巡察。」

translations.literal: In the eighth month of the first year of Tiansheng under Renzong, East and West Eight Works Offices with Inner Hall Commissioner and Gate Attendant Liu Yongchong etc. said: "Inside and outside eight wards newly placed figure-eight water inlets — connecting two waters into canals is very beneficial — fearing that where placed, wealthy and powerful may obstruct — request ordering inspection patrol."
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth month of the first year of Tiansheng, the East and West Eight Works Offices, together with Inner Hall commissioner and gate attendant Liu Yongchong and others, reported: "Figure-eight water inlets have newly been installed in eight wards inside and outside the city, and joining the two streams into the canals has proved very beneficial. We fear obstruction by the wealthy and powerful at the sites chosen and ask that patrols be ordered."

sentences.zh: 從之。

translations.literal: It was approved.
translations.idiomatic: The request was approved.

sentences.zh: 二年七月，內殿崇班、閣門祗候張君平等言：「准敕按視開封府界至南京、宿、亳諸州溝河形勢，疏決利害凡八事：一、商度地形，高下連屬，開治水勢，依尋古溝洫浚之，州縣計力役均定，置籍以主之。

translations.literal: In the seventh month of the second year, Inner Hall Honored Companion and Gate Attendant Zhang Junping etc. said: "Per edict inspecting Kaifeng Circuit to Nanjing, Su, Bo prefectures' canal terrain — dredging benefits and harms eight items total: First, assess terrain, high and low connected, manage water force, dredge following ancient canals; prefectures and counties calculate corvée evenly, keep registers to manage.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventh month of the second year, Zhang Junping, honored companion of the Inner Hall and gate attendant, and others reported: "By imperial order we inspected the canals from the Kaifeng circuit boundary to Nanjing and the prefectures of Su and Bo and set out eight points on dredging, benefit, and harm. First: assess the terrain and its connected rises and falls, manage the water's force, and dredge along the ancient canal lines; prefectures and counties should calculate corvée evenly and keep registers to oversee the work.

sentences.zh: 二、施工開治後，按視不如元計狀及水壅不行、有害民田者，按官吏之罪，令償其費。

translations.literal: Second, after construction dredging, if inspection finds not matching original plan or water blocked not flowing harming civilian fields — prosecute officials' crime, make them repay cost.
translations.idiomatic: Second: after dredging is completed, if inspection shows that the work falls short of the original plan, or that water is blocked and farmland is harmed, the responsible officials shall be prosecuted and made to repay the cost.

sentences.zh: 三、約束官吏，毋斂取夫眾財貨入己。

translations.literal: Third, constrain officials — do not gather corvée people's goods and wealth for oneself.
translations.idiomatic: Third: officials must be restrained from collecting corvée laborers' goods and money for themselves.

sentences.zh: 四、縣令佐、州守倅，有能勸課部民自用工開治不致水害者，敘為勞績，替日與家便官；

translations.literal: Fourth, county magistrates and assistants, prefectural prefects and vice-prefects — those able to urge subjects to use own labor dredging without causing water harm — record as merit, at replacement grant convenient official post near home;
translations.idiomatic: Fourth: county magistrates and assistants and prefectural prefects and vice-prefects who can urge their people to dredge with their own labor without causing flood damage shall have their service recorded as merit and, upon leaving office, be granted a convenient post near their home;

sentences.zh: 功績尤多，別議旌賞。

translations.literal: if merit especially great, separately discuss awards.
translations.idiomatic: those with especially great achievement shall receive separate commendation and reward.

sentences.zh: 五、民或于古河渠中修築堰堨，截水取魚，漸至澱淤，水潦暴集，河流不通，則致深害，乞嚴禁之。

translations.literal: Fifth, civilians sometimes in ancient canals build weirs and dikes, intercepting water to catch fish, gradually silting — when floods suddenly gather rivers do not flow, then causing deep harm — request strict prohibition.
translations.idiomatic: Fifth: when civilians build weirs and dikes in ancient river channels to trap water and catch fish, silt gradually accumulates; when sudden floods arrive the river cannot flow and great harm follows. We ask that this be strictly forbidden.

sentences.zh: 六、開治工畢，按行新舊廣深丈尺，以校工力。

translations.literal: Sixth, when dredging work completes, inspect new and old width and depth in chi, to verify labor.
translations.idiomatic: Sixth: when dredging is finished, inspect the new and old width and depth in chi to verify the labor performed.

sentences.zh: 以所出土，於溝河岸一步外築為堤埒。

translations.literal: With excavated earth, one pace outside canal banks build as dikes.
translations.idiomatic: The excavated earth should be piled one pace outside the canal banks to form dikes.

sentences.zh: 七、凡溝洫上廣一丈，則底廣八尺，其深四尺，地形高處或至五六尺，以此為率。

translations.literal: Seventh, wherever canals — top width one zhang, then bottom width eight chi, depth four chi; on high terrain up to five or six chi — use this as standard.
translations.idiomatic: Seventh: wherever a canal is one zhang wide at the top, its bottom should be eight chi wide and its depth four chi; on higher ground the depth may reach five or six chi. This should be the standard.

sentences.zh: 有廣狹不等處，折計之，則畢工之日，易於覆視。

translations.literal: Where width varies unequally, calculate proportionally — then on completion day, reinspection is easier.
translations.idiomatic: Where widths vary unevenly, they should be calculated proportionally so that reinspection will be easier on the day the work is completed.

sentences.zh: 八、古溝洫在民田中，久已淤平，今為賦籍而須開治者，據所占地步，為除其賦。」

translations.literal: Eighth, ancient canals in civilian fields long silted flat — now in tax registers yet needing dredging — according to occupied paces, exempt their tax."
translations.idiomatic: Eighth: ancient canals lying in farmland that have long silted level and are now on the tax rolls but must be reopened should have their tax remitted according to the land occupied."

sentences.zh: 詔令頒行。

translations.literal: An edict ordered promulgation.
translations.idiomatic: An edict ordered these regulations promulgated.

sentences.zh: 神宗熙甯元年三月，都水監言：「畿內溝河至多，而諸縣各役人夫開淘，十才二三，須二三年方可畢工。

translations.literal: In the third month of the first year of Xining, the Directorate said: "Capital-region canals are very numerous — yet each county separately employs laborers dredging, only two or three of ten — needing two or three years to complete.
translations.idiomatic: In the third month of the first year of Xining, the Directorate of Waterworks reported: "Canals within the capital region are extremely numerous, yet each county mobilizes labor separately for dredging, completing only two or three tenths of the work and needing two or three years to finish.

sentences.zh: 請令府界提點司選官，與縣官同定緊慢功料，據合差夫數，以五分夫，役十分工，依年分開淘，提點司通行點校。」

translations.literal: Request Circuit Intendant Office select officials, with county officials jointly set urgent and slow labor estimates, according to required corvée numbers — five parts corvée for ten parts work, dredge by yearly allotment, Intendant Office uniformly inspect."
translations.idiomatic: We ask that the Circuit Intendant Office select officials to work with county officials in setting urgent and routine labor estimates, assign corvée according to the required numbers, use five parts corvée for ten parts work, dredge by annual allotment, and have the Intendant Office inspect the whole effort."

sentences.zh: 從之。

translations.literal: It was approved.
translations.idiomatic: The proposal was approved.

sentences.zh: 二年閏十一月，詔以府界道路積水，妨民輸納，命都水監差官溝畎。

translations.literal: In intercalary eleventh month of the second year, an edict — due to circuit roads' accumulated water impeding civilian tax delivery — ordered the Directorate to dispatch officials for drainage channels.
translations.idiomatic: In the intercalary eleventh month of the second year, an edict noted that accumulated water on circuit roads was impeding tax delivery and ordered the Directorate of Waterworks to dispatch officials to open drainage channels.

sentences.zh: 元豐五年，詔開在京城濠，闊五十步，深一丈五尺，地脈不及者，至泉止。

translations.literal: In the fifth year of Yuanfeng, an edict ordered opening and dredging the capital moat — fifty paces wide, one zhang five chi deep; where earth strata did not reach, stop at spring water.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth year of Yuanfeng, an edict ordered the capital moat opened and dredged to a width of fifty paces and a depth of one zhang and five chi, stopping at spring water where the ground did not reach that depth.

sentences.zh: 徽宗大觀元年七月，以京城霖雨，水浸居民，道路不通，遣官分督疏導。

translations.literal: In the seventh month of the first year of Daguan under Huizong, due to capital continuous rain — water soaked residents, roads impassable — officials dispatched to supervise dredging separately.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventh month of the first year of Daguan, prolonged rain in the capital flooded residences and blocked the roads, and officials were dispatched to supervise dredging in separate districts.

sentences.zh: 是月又詔：「自京至八角鎮，積水妨行旅。

translations.literal: That same month another edict: "From capital to Bajiao Town, accumulated water impedes travelers.
translations.idiomatic: That same month another edict stated: "From the capital to Bajiao Town, standing water impedes travelers.

sentences.zh: 轉運司選官疏導，修治橋樑，毋使病涉。」

translations.literal: Transport Commissioner select officials to dredge, repair bridges — do not let crossing suffer."
translations.idiomatic: The transport commissioner should select officials to dredge the water and repair the bridges so that travelers are not put to hardship."

sentences.zh: 白河在唐州，南流入漢。

translations.literal: The Bai River is in Tang Prefecture, flowing south into the Han.
translations.idiomatic: The Bai River lies in Tang Prefecture and flows south into the Han.

sentences.zh: 太平興國三年正月，西京轉運使程能獻議，請自南陽下向口置堰，回水入石塘、沙河，合蔡河達于京師，以通湘潭之漕。

translations.literal: In the first month of the third year of Taiping Xingguo, Western Capital Transport Commissioner Cheng Neng submitted a proposal — request from Nanyang at Xiankou placing a weir, turning water into Shitang and Shahe, joining Cai River reaching the capital, to connect Xiangtan transport.
translations.idiomatic: In the first month of the third year of Taiping Xingguo, Cheng Neng, transport commissioner of the Western Capital, submitted a proposal to build a weir below Xiankou at Nanyang, turn the water into the Shitang and Shahe, join the Cai River, and reach the capital, thereby opening transport from Xiangtan.

sentences.zh: 詔發唐、鄧、汝、潁、許、蔡、陳、鄭丁夫及諸州兵，凡數萬人，以弓箭庫使王文寶、六宅使李繼隆、內作坊副使李神祐、劉承珪等護其役。

translations.literal: An edict mobilized corvée from Tang, Deng, Ru, Ying, Xu, Cai, Chen, Zheng and various prefecture troops — tens of thousands — with Bow and Arrow Treasury Commissioner Wang Wenbao, Six Residences Commissioner Li Jilong, Inner Workshops Deputy Commissioner Li Shenyou, Liu Chenggui etc. overseeing labor.
translations.idiomatic: An edict mobilized corvée laborers from Tang, Deng, Ru, Ying, Xu, Cai, Chen, and Zheng and troops from various prefectures, tens of thousands in all, and put Wang Wenbao, commissioner of the Bow and Arrow Treasury, Li Jilong, commissioner of the Six Residences, Li Shenyou, deputy commissioner of the Inner Workshops, Liu Chenggui, and others in charge of the work.

sentences.zh: 塹山陻穀，曆博望、羅渠、少柘山，凡百餘里，月餘，抵方城，地勢高，水不能至。

translations.literal: Cutting through mountains and filling valleys, passing Bowang, Luoditch, Shaotuo Mountain — over a hundred li — after more than a month reaching Fangcheng; terrain was high, water could not reach.
translations.idiomatic: They cut through mountains and filled valleys, passing Bowang, Luoditch, and Shaotuo Mountain for more than a hundred li. After more than a month they reached Fangcheng, but the ground there was high and water could not be brought up to it.

sentences.zh: 能獻復多役人以致水，然不可通漕運。

translations.literal: Neng again employed many laborers to bring water — yet transport could not be opened.
translations.idiomatic: Cheng Neng again employed many laborers to raise the water, but transport still could not be opened.

sentences.zh: 會山水暴漲，石堰壞，河不克就，卒堙廢焉。

translations.literal: When mountain floods suddenly rose, the stone weir broke, the river could not be completed, and was finally filled in and abandoned.
translations.idiomatic: Then mountain floods suddenly rose, the stone weir was destroyed, the canal could not be completed, and the project was finally filled in and abandoned.

sentences.zh: 端拱元年，供奉官閣門祗候閻文遜、苗忠俱上言：「開荊南城東漕河，至師子口入漢江，可通荊、峽漕路至襄州；

translations.literal: In the first year of Duangong, Presentation Officer and Gate Attendant Yan Wensun and Miao Zhong both submitted: "Open Jingnan east transport canal, to Shizi mouth entering Han River — can connect Jing and Xia transport route to Xiang Prefecture;
translations.idiomatic: In the first year of Duangong, Yan Wensun, presentation officer and gate attendant, and Miao Zhong both submitted memorials: "Open the eastern transport canal south of Jing, leading to Shizi mouth and into the Han River, and the grain route from Jing and the gorges to Xiang Prefecture can be connected;

sentences.zh: 又開古白河，可通襄、漢漕路至京。」

translations.literal: also open ancient Bai River — can connect Xiang and Han transport route to the capital."
translations.idiomatic: if the ancient Bai River is also opened, the grain route from Xiang and the Han to the capital can be connected as well."

sentences.zh: 詔八作使石全振往視之，遂發丁夫治荊南漕河至漢江，可勝二百斛重載，行旅者頗便，而古白河終不可開。

translations.literal: An edict ordered Eight Works Commissioner Shi Quanzhen to go inspect; corvée was then mobilized to dredge Jingnan transport canal to Han River — could support two-hundred-hu heavy loads; travelers found it quite convenient — yet ancient Bai River ultimately could not be opened.
translations.idiomatic: The court ordered Shi Quanzhen, commissioner of the Eight Works, to go inspect the site. Corvée laborers were then mobilized to dredge the Jingnan transport canal to the Han River. It could carry heavily laden boats of two hundred hu, and travelers found it quite convenient, but the ancient Bai River ultimately could not be opened.

sentences.zh: 三白渠在京兆涇陽縣。

translations.literal: The Sanbai Canal is in Jingyang County, Jingzhao.
translations.idiomatic: The Sanbai Canal is located in Jingyang County in Jingzhao.

sentences.zh: 淳化二年秋，縣民杜思淵上書言：「涇河內舊有石翣以堰水入白渠，溉雍、耀田，歲收三萬斛。

translations.literal: In autumn of the second year of Chunhua, county resident Du Siyuan submitted a memorial: "Within the Jing River there was formerly a stone barrage to dam water into the Bai Canal, irrigating Yong and Yao fields — annual harvest thirty thousand hu.
translations.idiomatic: In the autumn of the second year of Chunhua, Du Siyuan, a resident of the county, submitted a memorial stating: "Within the Jing River there was once a stone barrage that dammed water into the Bai Canal and irrigated the fields of Yong and Yao, yielding thirty thousand hu each year.

sentences.zh: 其後多歷年所，石翣壞，三白渠水少，溉田不足，民頗艱食。

translations.literal: Afterward many years passed, the stone barrage broke, Sanbai Canal water was little, irrigating fields insufficient, the people quite suffered shortage of food.
translations.idiomatic: Many years later the stone barrage failed, the Sanbai Canal carried too little water to irrigate the fields adequately, and the people faced real hardship in securing food.

sentences.zh: 乾德中，節度判官施繼業率民用梢穰、笆籬、棧木，截河為堰，壅水入渠。

translations.literal: In Qiande, regimentation adjutant Shi Jiye led the people using fascines, wicker fences, and pile timber, cutting off the river as a weir, damming water into the canal.
translations.idiomatic: During the Qiande era, military adjutant Shi Jiye mobilized the people to build a weir across the river from fascines, wicker fencing, and pile timber, forcing water into the canal.

sentences.zh: 緣渠之民，頗獲其利。

translations.literal: People along the canal quite obtained its benefit.
translations.idiomatic: The people living along the canal benefited considerably.

sentences.zh: 然凡遇暑雨，山水暴至，則堰輒壞。

translations.literal: Yet whenever summer rains were met, mountain water arrived violently, then the weir promptly broke.
translations.idiomatic: Yet whenever summer rains brought sudden mountain floods, the weir was destroyed almost at once.

sentences.zh: 至秋治堰，所用復取於民，民煩數役，終不能固。

translations.literal: When autumn came to repair the weir, materials used were again taken from the people; the people wearied of repeated corvée, ultimately could not be made solid.
translations.idiomatic: Each autumn the weir had to be repaired with materials once again levied from the people. Wearied by repeated corvée, they could never make the structure hold.

sentences.zh: 乞依古制，調丁夫修疊石翣，可得數十年不撓。

translations.literal: I beg according to ancient practice to mobilize corvée laborers to build a layered stone barrage — could obtain several decades without failing.
translations.idiomatic: I ask that, following the ancient practice, corvée laborers be mobilized to build a layered stone barrage that could stand firm for decades.

sentences.zh: 所謂暫勞永逸矣。」

translations.literal: What is called temporary toil, permanent ease."
translations.idiomatic: This is what people mean by a brief effort that brings lasting benefit."

sentences.zh: 詔從之，遣將作監丞周約己等董其役，以用功尤大，不能就而止。

translations.literal: The edict approved; dispatched Assistant Director of the Directorate of Imperial Manufactories Zhou Yueji and others to superintend the labor — because labor requirement was especially great, could not be completed and was halted.
translations.idiomatic: The court approved the proposal and dispatched Zhou Yueji, assistant director of the Directorate of Imperial Manufactories, and others to oversee the work, but the labor required proved too vast and the project was abandoned before completion.

sentences.zh: 正月，度支判官梁鼎、陳堯叟上《鄭白渠利害》：「按舊史，鄭渠元引涇水，自仲山西抵瓠口，並北山東注洛，三百餘里，溉田四萬頃，畝收一鐘。

translations.literal: In the first month, Revenue Section adjutants Liang Ding and Chen Yaosou submitted "On the Benefits and Harms of the Zheng and Bai Canals": "According to old histories, the Zheng Canal originally drew Jing water from Zhong Mountain west to Hugou, running east along the northern hills to pour into the Luo for more than three hundred li, irrigating forty thousand qing and yielding one zhong per mu.
translations.idiomatic: In the first month, Liang Ding and Chen Yaosou, adjutants of the Revenue Section, submitted "On the Benefits and Harms of the Zheng and Bai Canals": "According to old histories, the Zheng Canal originally drew Jing water from Zhong Mountain west to Hugou and ran east along the northern hills into the Luo for more than three hundred li, irrigating forty thousand qing and yielding one zhong per mu.

sentences.zh: 白渠亦引涇水，起穀口，入櫟陽，注渭水，長二百餘里，溉田四千五百頃。

translations.literal: The Bai Canal also drew Jing water, rising at Gukou, entering Liyang, and pouring into the Wei for more than two hundred li, irrigating four thousand five hundred qing.
translations.idiomatic: The Bai Canal also drew Jing water from Gukou through Liyang into the Wei for more than two hundred li and irrigated four thousand five hundred qing.

sentences.zh: 兩渠溉田凡四萬四千五百頃，今所存者不及二千頃，皆近代改修渠堰，浸隳舊防，繇是灌溉之利，絕少於古矣。

translations.literal: The two canals together irrigated forty-four thousand five hundred qing; what survives today is less than two thousand qing, all because in recent times channel works and weirs were altered and old defenses gradually ruined, so irrigation benefit is far less than in antiquity.
translations.idiomatic: Together the two canals irrigated forty-four thousand five hundred qing; what survives today is less than two thousand qing, because recent alterations to channels and weirs have gradually destroyed the old defenses and irrigation benefit is far less than in antiquity.

sentences.zh: 鄭渠難為興工，今請遣使先詣三白渠行視，復修舊跡。」

translations.literal: The Zheng Canal would be hard to restore; we now ask that envoys first be sent to inspect the Sanbai Canal and restore the old traces."
translations.idiomatic: The Zheng Canal would be hard to restore; we now ask that envoys first be sent to inspect the Sanbai Canal and restore the old traces."

sentences.zh: 於是詔大理寺丞皇甫選、光祿寺丞何亮乘傳經度。

translations.literal: Thereupon an edict ordered Court of Judicial Review Assistant Director Huangfu Xuan and Court of Imperial Sacrifices Assistant Director He Liang to travel on imperial commission and survey the works.
translations.idiomatic: Thereupon the court ordered Huangfu Xuan, assistant director of the Court of Judicial Review, and He Liang, assistant director of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices, to travel on imperial commission and survey the works.

sentences.zh: 選等使還，言：周覽鄭渠之制，用功最大。

translations.literal: When Xuan and his party returned from their mission, they reported: having toured the Zheng Canal system, its labor requirement is greatest.
translations.idiomatic: When Xuan and his party returned from their mission, they reported that, having toured the Zheng Canal system in full, restoring it would demand the greatest labor of all.

sentences.zh: 並仲山而東，鑿斷岡阜，首尾三百餘里，連亙山足，岸壁頹壞，堙廢已久。

translations.literal: From Zhong Mountain eastward, cutting through ridges and mounds, head to tail over three hundred li, running continuously along the mountain foot — bank walls collapsed and ruined, filled in and abandoned long ago.
translations.idiomatic: It runs east from Zhong Mountain, cutting through ridges and hillocks for more than three hundred li along the mountain's base. Its banks have long since collapsed, and the canal has been filled in and abandoned for many years.

sentences.zh: 度其制置之始，涇河平淺，直入渠口。

translations.literal: Considering when it was first constructed, the Jing River was level and shallow, flowing straight into the canal mouth.
translations.idiomatic: When the canal was first built, the Jing River was level and shallow and flowed directly into the canal mouth.

sentences.zh: 暨年代浸遠，涇河陡深，水勢漸下，與渠口相懸，水不能至。

translations.literal: As years gradually passed, the Jing River grew steep and deep, the water's force gradually descending — suspended above the canal mouth, water could not reach.
translations.idiomatic: As the years passed, the Jing River cut deeper and deeper, its current falling lower and lower until it stood far above the canal mouth and water could no longer be brought in.

sentences.zh: 峻崖之處，渠岸摧毀，荒廢歲久，實難致力。

translations.literal: Where cliffs were steep, canal banks were destroyed; abandoned for many years — truly difficult to apply effort.
translations.idiomatic: Where the cliffs are steep the banks have been destroyed, and after so many years of neglect it would truly be hard to restore the work.

sentences.zh: 其三白渠溉涇陽、櫟陽、高陵、雲陽、三原、富平六縣田三千八百五十餘頃，此渠衣食之源也，望令增築堤堰，以固護之。

translations.literal: The Sanbai Canal irrigates more than 3,850 qing of fields in six counties — Jingyang, Liyang, Gaoling, Yunyang, Sanyuan, and Fuping. This canal is the source of food and clothing. I hope an order will be given to raise dikes and weirs to fortify and protect it.
translations.idiomatic: The Sanbai Canal irrigates more than 3,850 qing of land in six counties — Jingyang, Liyang, Gaoling, Yunyang, Sanyuan, and Fuping. It is the source of their food and clothing. We ask that dikes and weirs be raised to strengthen and protect it.

sentences.zh: 舊設節水斗門一百七十有六，皆壞，請悉繕完。

translations.literal: Formerly installed water-conserving sluice gates numbered one hundred seventy-six — all broken; I request all be fully repaired.
translations.idiomatic: Of the 176 water-conserving sluice gates once installed, not one remains intact. We ask that all of them be fully repaired.

sentences.zh: 渠口舊有六石門，謂之「洪門」，今亦隤圮，若復議興置，則其功甚大，且欲就近度其岸勢，別開渠口，以通水道。

translations.literal: At the canal mouth there were formerly six stone gates called "Hong Gate" — now also collapsed. If reconstruction is again proposed, the labor would be very great. Moreover, I wish to survey nearby the bank's configuration and open a separate canal mouth to connect the watercourse.
translations.idiomatic: At the canal mouth there were once six stone gates known as the "Hong Gate", but they too have collapsed. Rebuilding them would require enormous labor. We would rather survey the nearby banks and open a new canal mouth to restore the watercourse.

sentences.zh: 歲令渠官行視，岸之缺薄，水之淤填，即時浚治。

translations.literal: Each year order canal officials to make inspection rounds; where banks are deficient or thin, or water is silted and filled in — dredge and repair immediately.
translations.idiomatic: Canal officials should inspect the works each year and dredge or repair at once wherever banks are weak or channels silted up.

sentences.zh: 嚴豪民盜水之禁。

translations.literal: Strictly enforce the prohibition against powerful families stealing water.
translations.idiomatic: The prohibition against powerful families stealing water should be strictly enforced.

sentences.zh: 涇河中舊有石堰，修廣皆百步，捍水雄壯，謂之「將軍翣」，廢壞已久。

translations.literal: Within the Jing River there was formerly a stone weir, length and width each one hundred bu, holding back water with imposing strength — called the "General Barrage" — ruined and abandoned long ago.
translations.idiomatic: Within the Jing River there was once a stone weir a hundred bu long and a hundred bu wide, a mighty structure that held back the water and was called the "General Barrage". It has long lain in ruins.

sentences.zh: 杜思淵嘗請興修，而功不克就。

translations.literal: Du Siyuan once requested restoration, but the work could not be completed.
translations.idiomatic: Du Siyuan once petitioned for its restoration, but the work could not be brought to completion.

sentences.zh: 其後止造木堰，凡用梢樁萬一千三百餘數，歲出於緣渠之民。

translations.literal: Afterward only wooden weirs were built, using in all more than eleven thousand three hundred pile stakes, supplied each year by the people along the canal.
translations.idiomatic: After that only wooden weirs were built, requiring more than eleven thousand three hundred pile stakes each year, all supplied by the people living along the canal.

sentences.zh: 涉夏水潦，木堰遽壞，漂流散失，至秋，復率民以葺之，數斂重困，無有止息。

translations.literal: Through summer floods, the wooden weirs promptly broke, drifted away and were lost. When autumn came, the people were again led to repair them — levied repeatedly, heavily burdened, without cease.
translations.idiomatic: Summer floods destroyed the wooden weirs almost at once, scattering the timbers downstream. Each autumn the people were mobilized to rebuild them, taxed again and again until the burden became unbearable and never ended.

sentences.zh: 欲令自今溉田既畢，命水工拆堰木置於岸側，可充二三歲修堰之用。

translations.literal: I wish to order that from now on, once irrigation is finished, water workers dismantle the weir timber and place it on the bank side — sufficient for two or three years of weir repair.
translations.idiomatic: From now on, once irrigation is finished, water workers should dismantle the weir timber and store it on the bank, enough to supply two or three years of repairs.

sentences.zh: 所役緣渠之民，計田出丁，凡調萬三千人。

translations.literal: The people along the canal who serve corvée — calculating by fields to supply laborers — total thirteen thousand men mobilized.
translations.idiomatic: The people along the canal who perform corvée, assessed by field and household, number thirteen thousand men in all.

sentences.zh: 疏渠造堰，各獲其利，固不憚其勞也。

translations.literal: Dredging canals and building weirs — each obtains benefit; they naturally do not shrink from the labor.
translations.idiomatic: Because dredging the canal and building the weir benefits everyone, they will not begrudge the labor.

sentences.zh: 選能吏司其事，置暑于涇陽縣側，以時行視，往復甚便。

translations.literal: Select capable officials to manage the matter; establish an office beside Jingyang County for timely inspection — going back and forth is very convenient.
translations.idiomatic: Capable officials should be chosen to manage the work, with an office established beside Jingyang County so that inspections can be made regularly and travel back and forth kept convenient.

sentences.zh: 又言：

translations.literal: They further reported:
translations.idiomatic: They also reported:

sentences.zh: 鄧、許、陳、潁、蔡、宿、亳七州之地，有公私閒田凡三百五十一處，合二十二萬餘頃，民力不能盡耕。

translations.literal: In the lands of seven prefectures — Deng, Xu, Chen, Ying, Cai, Su, and Bo — there are public and private idle fields totaling 351 locations, together more than 220,000 qing; popular strength cannot fully cultivate them.
translations.idiomatic: In the seven prefectures of Deng, Xu, Chen, Ying, Cai, Su, and Bo there are 351 tracts of public and private idle land totaling more than 220,000 qing — more than the people can fully cultivate.

sentences.zh: 皆漢、魏以來，召信臣、杜詩、杜預、任峻、司馬宣王、鄧艾等立制墾辟之地。

translations.literal: All are lands where from Han and Wei times Zhao Xinxin, Du Shi, Du Yu, Ren Jun, Sima the Lord of Xuan, Deng Ai, and others established systems of reclamation and opening.
translations.idiomatic: All were lands opened under systems established since Han and Wei times by Zhao Xinxin, Du Shi, Du Yu, Ren Jun, Sima the Lord of Xuan, Deng Ai, and others.

sentences.zh: 內南陽界鑿山開道，疏通河水，散入唐、鄧、襄三州以溉田。

translations.literal: Within the Nanyang region, mountains were cut and passages opened, river water dredged and channeled, dispersed into Tang, Deng, and Xiang prefectures to irrigate fields.
translations.idiomatic: Within the Nanyang region, mountains were cut through and channels opened to dredge river water and distribute it into Tang, Deng, and Xiang prefectures for irrigation.

sentences.zh: 又諸處陂塘防埭，大者長三十里至五十里，闊五丈至八丈，高一丈五尺至二丈。

translations.literal: Also at various places reservoir ponds and protective dikes — the large ones thirty to fifty li long, five to eight zhang wide, one zhang five chi to two zhang high.
translations.idiomatic: At various sites there are reservoir ponds and protective dikes; the largest run thirty to fifty li long, five to eight zhang wide, and one and a half to two zhang high.

sentences.zh: 其溝渠，大者長五十里至百里，闊三丈至五丈，深一丈至一丈五尺，可行小舟。

translations.literal: Their ditches and canals — the large ones fifty to one hundred li long, three to five zhang wide, one to one and a half zhang deep — can carry small boats.
translations.idiomatic: Their ditches and canals, the largest of them fifty to one hundred li long, three to five zhang wide, and one to one and a half zhang deep, can carry small boats.

sentences.zh: 臣等周行歷覽，若皆增築陂堰，勞費頗甚，欲堤防未壞可興水利者，先耕二萬餘頃，他處漸圖建置。

translations.literal: We traveled throughout and surveyed on foot. If all reservoir dikes were raised, labor and expense would be considerable. Where dikes are not yet ruined and waterworks can be undertaken, I wish first to cultivate more than 20,000 qing; elsewhere gradually plan construction.
translations.idiomatic: We traveled throughout and inspected the region on foot. Rebuilding every reservoir and dike would require enormous labor and expense. Where the dikes are still intact and waterworks can be restored, we propose first to put more than 20,000 qing under cultivation and gradually develop the rest.

sentences.zh: 時著作佐郎孫冕總監三白渠，詔冕依選等奏行之。

translations.literal: At the time Assistant Editorial Director Sun Mian supervised the Sanbai Canal overall; an edict ordered Sun Mian to implement Xuan and his party's memorial.
translations.idiomatic: At that time Assistant Editorial Director Sun Mian was put in overall charge of the Sanbai Canal, and the court ordered him to carry out the recommendations submitted by Xuan and his colleagues.

sentences.zh: 後自仲山之南，移治涇陽縣。

translations.literal: Later, from south of Zhong Mountain, administration was relocated to Jingyang County.
translations.idiomatic: Later the administrative seat was moved from south of Zhong Mountain to Jingyang County.

sentences.zh: 其七州之田，令選于鄧州募民耕墾，皆免賦入。

translations.literal: As for the seven prefectures' fields, Xuan was ordered to go to Deng Prefecture to recruit people to farm and reclaim — all exempt from tax levies.
translations.idiomatic: For the fields in those seven prefectures, Xuan was ordered to go to Deng Prefecture to recruit settlers to farm and reclaim the land, with all tax levies waived.

sentences.zh: 復令選等舉一人，與鄧州通判同掌其事。

translations.literal: Xuan and his party were again ordered to recommend one person to administer the matter jointly with the Deng Prefecture vice prefect.
translations.idiomatic: Xuan and his colleagues were also ordered to recommend one person to manage the project together with the vice prefect of Deng Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 選與亮分路按察，未幾而罷。

translations.literal: Xuan and Liang inspected separately by different routes; before long the arrangement was abolished.
translations.idiomatic: Xuan and Liang conducted inspections by separate routes, but before long the arrangement was discontinued.

sentences.zh: 景德三年，鹽鐵副使林特、度支副使馬景盛陳關中河渠之利，請遣官行鄭、白渠，興修古制。

translations.literal: In the third year of Jingde, Vice Commissioner of Salt and Iron Lin Te and Vice Commissioner of Revenue Ma Jingsheng presented the benefits of Guanzhong rivers and canals, requesting officials be dispatched to conduct the Zheng and Bai canals and restore the ancient system.
translations.idiomatic: In the third year of Jingde, Lin Te, vice commissioner of salt and iron, and Ma Jingsheng, vice commissioner of revenue, described the benefits of the rivers and canals of Guanzhong and asked that officials be sent to survey the Zheng and Bai canals and restore the ancient system.

sentences.zh: 乃詔太常博士尚賓乘傳經度，率丁夫治之。

translations.literal: An edict then ordered Chamberlain for Ceremonials Doctor Shang Bin to travel on imperial dispatch to survey and direct, leading corvée laborers to dredge it.
translations.idiomatic: The court then ordered Shang Bin, a doctor of the Chamberlain for Ceremonials, to travel on imperial commission to survey the works and lead corvée laborers in repairing them.

sentences.zh: 賓言：「鄭渠久廢不可復，今自介公廟回白渠洪口直東南，合舊渠以畎涇河，灌富平、櫟陽、高陵等縣，經久可以不竭。」

translations.literal: Shang reported: "The Zheng Canal has long been abandoned and cannot be restored. Now from Jie Gong Temple, return to the Bai Canal Hong mouth due southeast, join the old canal to draw the Jing River, irrigating Fuping, Liyang, Gaoling and other counties — over time it can be inexhaustible."
translations.idiomatic: Shang reported: "The Zheng Canal has long been abandoned and cannot be restored. From Jie Gong Temple we can return to the Hong mouth of the Bai Canal and run due southeast, joining the old canal to draw off the Jing River and irrigate Fuping, Liyang, Gaoling, and other counties. Over time the supply should not fail."

sentences.zh: 工既畢而水利饒足，民獲數倍。

translations.literal: The work was completed and water supply was abundant; the people gained several times their former yield.
translations.idiomatic: When the work was finished the water supply was abundant, and the people reaped several times their former harvest.
